title: Add exemplar shedder sidecar to limit hotpath tracing costs
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Ingress and application-side tracing hooks remain a significant CPU and allocation hotspot in high-QPS services. Current tail-based and adaptive sampling improvements reduce trace volume but still require encoding spans and allocating buffers on the hot path for many requests that end up unsampled. That per-request overhead inflates 95/99th latency and increases cost for Dedicated clusters.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight "exemplar shedder" sidecar that sits next to the ingress or service process and makes a pre-sampling decision using ultra-cheap signals. The shedder receives tiny telemetry probes (a few bytes) synchronously on the hot path, applies a per-shard micro-reservoir + burst-sensitive backoff policy, and returns one of three outcomes: 1) mark for immediate full sampling, 2) mark as candidate and enqueue an async fetch/collect path, 3) ignore (no encoding or span allocations). Full trace pull and enrichment happen out-of-band to avoid hotpath work. The sidecar is non-privileged, written in Rust, and designed to have <200ns median CPU on the request path and a tiny heap (<= 512 KB).

Why this is different: Unlike full prefilter approaches that still require span encoding or complex prefilters, the exemplar shedder treats the hot path as a minimal decision surface and defers all heavy work. It complements existing tail-sampling controllers by reducing the volume they need to evaluate, and it provides a stable per-tenant budget guardrail for Dedicated nodes.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath per-request CPU allocations for instrumented endpoints reduced by >=35% compared to current tracer baseline
P99 added latency from tracing instrumentation remains <1ms at 99th on representative 95th-percentile load profiles
End-to-end sampled trace fidelity for alerted incidents preserved (no regression on critical-failure trace coverage)
Sidecar runs with no special host privileges; deployment manifests for Dedicated and Private included
Design doc and implementation tested on canary service with traffic shadowing and automated regression benchmarks

Prototype sidecar in Rust with minimal probe API (Omar)
Micro-reservoir algorithm: implement burst-sensitive hedging and tenant budget (Eng team)
Benchmark harness: synthetic QPS driver + real production trace replays (SRE)
Integrate async trace pull pipeline (worker pool + rate limiter)
Security review & RBAC integration for Private deployments
Kubernetes manifests + Helm chart for Dedicated/Private
Canary rollout with shadowing and perf dashboards in Console

2026-03-05 Engineering review: raised concern about cross-service clock sync when deciding exemplar eviction; added TTL-based conservative policy.
2026-03-08 SRE note: benchmark harness will replay a subset of production header fingerprints; will provide 1M-rps trace subset by 2026-03-10.
2026-03-10 Design feedback from Alex Martinez (Platform): ensure sidecar implements a small circuit-breaker to avoid amplifying downstream failures; added to tasks.
